Speaking to Fox News' Fox and Friends, the president said Israel no longer needed the funding.
Now, as far as paying Israel, the Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4 billion a year,
and we made a deal months ago that we're stopping.
It was not clear what specific funding Trump was referring to,
a memorandum of understanding that provides $3.8 billion of military aid was set to expire in 2028.
Trump also said that Israel can continue to buy whatever they want.
Asked about the timing of the announcement on election day, Trump said it wasn't a good talking point,
acknowledging that some Democrats were using the financial support to criticize Republicans.
Franco, Ordonez, NPR News.
Flood warnings remain up for much of Florida's Atlantic coast after devastating storms.
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has declared states of emergency in eight Florida counties.
That has allowed election officials to move dozens of polling stations because of high water or damage.
David Becker leads the Center for Election Innovation and Research.
The group promotes election integrity and security.
He notes that about 60 million Americans have already cast early ballots and few problems have been reported.
He also says voters should not be concerned about reports of law enforcement or ICE agents being sent to polling stations.
If there were even a single deployment of ICE or troops near a polling place, even accidentally,
the courts would stop it immediately and lawyers are ready to stop it.
So voters should feel very confident.
He spoke to NPR's Morning Edition.
Polls open this hour in Washington state and Alaska.
Alaska's U.S. Senate race between incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan and Democratic challenger Mary Peltola may not be called for weeks.
The state uses ranked choice voting.
But as Alaska public media's Liz Ruskin explains, that's not why the wait takes so long.
Alaska is about three times the size of France with few roads.
Mail is slow. By law, the state allows up to 15 days for ballots to arrive.
If Peltola or Sullivan wins more than 50 percent of the vote, that's it.
They've won. With four people on the ballot, though, it could come down to ranked choices.
That's like an instant runoff.
It takes just seconds for a computer to eliminate the losing candidate and count the next choices on those ballots.
But the state only does it once the 15 days are up.
The Associated Press could call the race well before November 18 or if it's close, not.
For NPR News, I'm Liz Ruskin in Anchorage.
This is NPR.
The White House says that First Lady Melania Trump will host officials from Ukraine and Russia at the White House.
Trump administration officials say Mrs.
Trump helped broker a recent cease fire in the Ukrainian town of Olesky.
Civilians there were allowed to evacuate.
Those who remained were given humanitarian aid.
Mrs. Trump is scheduled to speak about the cease fire Thursday morning.
This development comes as President Trump's special envoy, Steve Whitcoff, says the U.S.
will mediate talks between Ukraine and Russia next week.
The meeting will be in Abu Dhabi. Ukraine's president has confirmed the talks.
Thousands of U.S. military veterans are paying higher mortgage costs.
NPR's Quill Lawrence reports that's as a result of the Trump administration canceling a key program.
Most Americans have options if they fall behind on their mortgage.
Lenders offer loan modifications that almost always lower the monthly payment or keep it the same.
But last year, the V.A. abruptly ended a program to do that.
And an NPR investigation found 63 percent of V.A.'s loan mods since then raised the cost on veterans.
Army vet Scott Boyd fell behind after going into a V.A. hospital to treat PTSD.
The only way to keep his home was a new loan that's nearly $1,200 higher per month.
After everything that I've done, like for this country and the things that I've been through,
it's just like I felt so defeated.
Our investigation found thousands of vets are paying more than $700 more every month.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
And I'm Cora Vekulman, NPR News in Washington.
